chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man permits his slave to engage in trade, and debt comes to be upon him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If he permitted him to incur debt, then the debt is upon his master. And if he did not permit him to incur debt, then there is nothing upon the master, and the slave is sought out (to pay) the debt.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for the debt if a slave incurs it while trading with the master's permission?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of vicarious liability in Islamic commercial law, distinguishing between explicit permission to incur debt (making the master liable) and mere permission to trade (leaving the slave personally liable). It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the master's consent as the determining factor for financial responsibility, ensuring clarity in master-slave economic transactions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man permits his owned slave regarding the business, so debts come to be upon him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘If it was such that it was permitted to him to incur debts, so the debts would be upon his master, and if there did not happen to be a permission for him that he incurs debts, so there would not be anything upon the master, and the slave would have to work regarding the debts’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from abu Basir who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who authorizes his slave to do business but he becomes indebted. He (the Imam) said, Tf his master had authorized him to borrow; then he is responsible for the debts, but if he had not authorized him to borrow, he is not responsible for anything but the slave is made to work to pay the debts.’”
